headline_marked: [[Anthropic's Claude Code launches 'artifacts']] for live, shareable web pages from coding sessions
headline: Anthropic's Claude Code launches 'artifacts' for live, shareable web pages from coding sessions
summary: Claude Code's new 'artifacts' feature transforms coding session outputs into interactive, private web pages, enhancing collaboration for Team and Enterprise users. It integrates with Claude Design for a seamless AI-driven development loop.
details: Anthropic has shipped "artifacts" in Claude Code, allowing users to turn coding session work into live, shareable web pages. These are interactive web pages at private URLs that update as the session progresses, generated directly from the coding context.

Unlike generic canvases, these artifacts are views into the specific work the AI agent just completed, reflecting files touched, changes made, and tests run. The feature is currently in beta for Team and Enterprise plans, requiring users to be signed in.

Artifacts are private by default, shared explicitly with teammates, and viewable only by authenticated organization members. Admins have control over org-level toggles, role-based scoping, retention policies, and compliance API visibility.

This launch follows a major overhaul of Claude Design two days prior, introducing design system imports, canvas editing, and a /design-sync command. These features directly connect to the Claude Code workflow, bridging the gap between design and code.

Users can now import design systems into Claude Design, generate assets using their components, and edit elements directly on the canvas without regenerating. The /design-sync command allows pushing code changes back to Claude Design or pulling design systems into repos.

Artifacts enable new workflows like "Show Don't Tell" PR reviews, live incident pages, and sprint visibility dashboards, providing full context without manual write-ups. The "Design Handoff Loop" keeps the entire process within one AI system.

The core problem artifacts solve is making AI coding session outputs visible to others, collapsing the manual communication step. Boris Cherny, creator of Claude Code, emphasizes this visibility for managing thousands of AI agents.

Anthropic's competitors like Codex, Cursor, and Windsurf lack a live artifact system for shareable web pages or a direct pipeline to a first-party design tool with the same AI backbone. This positions Anthropic uniquely.
Artifacts and /design-sync represent Anthropic's strategy: for the AI coding agent to own the full development loop from design to deployment and communication.
